traceability.notes:
The story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION (Requirement Content Validation) describes deep validation of @req annotations against the actual content of referenced story files. This is implemented by the `valid-req-reference` rule in src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts, which reads each referenced story file, extracts all requirement IDs using a general `REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+` regex applied over the entire markdown content, caches these IDs per file, and validates every @req annotation against that cache.
Core functionality is covered: if the requirement ID from an @req annotation does not appear in the story file’s extracted ID set, the rule reports a `reqMissing` error with both the requirement ID and story path. Various requirement formats and structures are handled because the parsing is not tied to specific sections; it simply scans the whole document. This is demonstrated in tests with both standard story requirements (e.g., `**REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE**` in docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md) and bullet-list requirements (tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md). Caching is implemented via a Map keyed by resolved story paths, avoiding re-parsing.
The rule integrates with existing annotation and file validation logic by reusing the comment-based scanning approach (processing @story and @req lines from JSDoc or line comments) and by adding path validation and error handling around file resolution and reading. Error messages are clear and specific (`Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'` and `Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'`), with tests asserting both message IDs and contextual data.
Error handling is robust: path traversal and absolute paths are explicitly rejected, and file read failures are caught so they do not crash ESLint. Instead, they lead to controlled validation outcomes. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md directly references this story, explains the behavior, and provides examples of correct and incorrect usage.
Given the implemented rule logic, its dedicated tests, its integration into the plugin exports and configs, and the accompanying documentation, all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied. Therefore the story is assessed as PASSED.
